transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve gotten to where I’ll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor at work. I’ll switch clients, say the blade’s missing, hide it in the drawer. And if I can’t get out of it, I’m shaking through the whole shave.
What is the main thought or fear going through your mind when you have to use the straight razor?

I keep thinking I’m going to slip and seriously cut the client, or cut myself badly. I know it’s just a tool—I trained with it—but seeing it open at my station makes it feel dangerous in a way clippers don’t.
Do these thoughts or mental images of cutting someone pop into your mind even when you are away from the razor?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed those images coming up when I’m away from work.
How long has this intense fear of using the straight razor been going on?
It’s been about 11 months now, since the arguments with the shop owner about the straight-razor shave package started.

inference_history.note: Initial assessment: Patient presents with intense avoidance and anxiety specifically related to using a straight razor at work. Differential includes specific phobia (e.g., sharp objects), obsessive-compulsive disorder (harm obsessions), social anxiety disorder (performance anxiety/fear of shaking in front of clients), and post-traumatic stress disorder.
